item.title: Lindsay Clancy was failed by our warped understanding of motherhood | Moira Donegan
item.description:
One of the things that I find very interesting about the Lindsay Clancy case is that it’s a complex fact pattern. There’s a fake thing that happens in psychiatry in which it’s assumed that people are capable of pure, easy diagnoses and that drugs are extremely effective. Neither one is true. If you spend any time with psychiatrists or with the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) — or people who have dealt with psychiatrists, the DSM, or medication — you would know it’s probably the least-developed area of all medicine. Psychiatry is incredibly vague. Basically, these things are diagnosed based on checklists and a person’s self-reported symptoms.
